prompt: An analyst discovers that a company's stock consistently earns positive abnormal returns in the three days following its quarterly earnings announcements. This finding most directly challenges which form of market efficiency?
explanation: Earnings announcements are public information. If prices do not fully and immediately reflect this public information — allowing investors to earn abnormal returns by acting on it — the market fails the semi-strong form test, which requires that prices reflect all publicly available information. Weak-form efficiency relates only to past price and volume data (technical analysis), not earnings news. Strong-form efficiency relates to non-public (insider) information. Since earnings announcements are public, this anomaly tests the semi-strong form specifically.
